_comment: Risk tiers, roster, and filtering policy for the review factory. This file is DATA:
prepare_review.py reads it and never hardcodes any of these values, so the roster can be
adjusted from cost/yield evidence (score_run.py's cost-per-finding-per-specialist) without
touching code. Thresholds follow Cloudflare's published tiers.
Tier assessment order (first match wins), implemented in assess_risk_tier():
1. any changed path matches security_sensitive_globs  -> full  (risk beats size)
2. lines > full.min_lines OR files > full.min_files    -> full
3. lines <= trivial.max_lines AND files <= trivial.max_files -> trivial
4. lines <= lite.max_lines AND files <= lite.max_files       -> lite
Rule 5 catches the 21-50-file, <=100-line case: many files touched is itself a risk signal.
_role_focus_comment: An empty focus list means 'no narrowing' — the role reviews every kept file.
A non-empty list is FOCUS, not a hard filter: the role still sees the full file list in its
brief, but its patches and attention are scoped to matches. Scoping is the single biggest
lever on both cost and noise (Cloudflare's per-file patch scoping).
_boundary_tags_comment: Tag names stripped (case-insensitively, with or without attributes, opening and closing)
from PR titles, bodies, and comments before they reach shared-context.md. A PR description
is attacker-controlled text; without this a PR body could impersonate a system turn and
redirect a specialist. Stripping happens in code, not in a prompt asking nicely.
